records.sourceHebrew: מַאי ״כִּי זֶה כׇּל הָאָדָם״? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה. רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: שָׁקוּל זֶה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא לִצְווֹת לָזֶה.
records.sourceEnglish: What is meant by “for this is the whole of man”? Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: The entire world was created only for the sake of this one. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This one is equal in worth to the entire world. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says—and some say that Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma says: The entire world was created only to accompany this one.
records.targetHebrew: הָאָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה צָרִיךְ לְצַוְותָא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו:): "כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא לְצַוֵּת לָזֶה", שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ דְּהוּא צָרִיךְ לְצַוְותָא דִּנְבְרָאִים. וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֵירוּבִין נד.): "הַמְהַלֵּךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ וְאֵין לוֹ לְוָיָה יַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה", וְהָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה כֻּלּוֹ נִקְרָא הִילוּךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה כא.) עַל פָּסוּק "בְּהִתְהַלֶּכְךָ תַּנְחֶה וְגוֹמֵר" – בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה. וּכְשֶׁאֵין לוֹ צַוְותָא יַעֲסֹק בַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁהוּא דְּפוּס מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית וְשֶׁל כָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה א, וְנִמְצָא יֵשׁ לוֹ צַוְותָא שֶׁל כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה וְכָל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ.
records.targetEnglish: A person in this world needs companionship, as they said in Berakhot 6b: “The entire world was created only to accompany this one.” We learn from this that he needs the companionship of created beings. And our Sages of blessed memory said in Eruvin 54a: “One who walks on the road and has no escort should occupy himself with Torah.” This entire world is called walking on the road, as our Sages expounded in Sotah 21a on “When you walk, it will guide you”: this refers to this world. When a person has no companionship, he should occupy himself with Torah, for Torah is the pattern of the work of Creation and of all created beings, as they said in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 1. He thus has the companionship of the entire creation and of the whole world.
records.explanation: Rav Tzadok develops the specific phrase “to accompany this one”: the created world supplies companionship, and Torah can supply that companionship because it contains the pattern of all creation. The passage therefore explains the transition from the Gemara’s statement about the world to the practical instruction to occupy oneself with Torah when alone.

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This one is equal in worth to the entire world. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says—and some say that Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma says: The entire world was created only to accompany this one.
records.targetHebrew: וְ״הַכֹּל שָׁב אֶל הֶעָפָר״ (קֹהֶלֶת שָׁם) הוּא סוֹד הַתְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁחוֹזֵר לַמָּקוֹר וְזֶהוּ נֶגֶד אֶחָד בְּתִשְׁרֵי רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לִשְׁמִטִּין וּלְיוֹבְלוֹת שֶׁהוּא זְמַן קְדֻשַּׁת הָאָרֶץ, דְּיוּכְלוּ לְהַכְנִיס הַקְּדוּשָׁה גַּם בַּדּוֹמְמִים וִיסוֹד הֶעָפָר זֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַתְּשׁוּבָה, דְּמַכִּיר שִׁפְלוּתוֹ וְנַפְשׁוֹ כְּעָפָר לַכֹּל תִּהְיֶה וְעַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הַמְּרִירוּת לִמְאוֹס בְּחַיָּיו בְּהַכִּירוֹ גֹּודֶל חֶטְאוֹ לַהַמְרוֹת רְצוֹן מֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עַד שֶׁיְּבוּטַּל גַּם גּוּף הָעַפְרִי בַּמְּצִיאוּת ״מִפְּנֵי פַּחַד ה׳ וּמֵהֲדַר גְּאוֹנוֹ״ (יְשַׁעְיָה ב:י) וּבָזֶה יְתוּקַּן יְסוֹד הֶעָפָר וְהַדּוֹמֵם שֶׁבְּכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ דְּהַכֹּל כָּלוּל בָּאָדָם, שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ נִבְרָא בִּשְׁבִילוֹ וּלְצַוּוֹת לוֹ, כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) וּבְתִיקּוּנוֹ וּשְׁלֵימוּתוֹ נִשְׁלָם כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ
records.targetEnglish: “And everything returns to the dust” is the mystery of repentance, which returns to the source. This corresponds to the first of Tishrei, the New Year for the sabbatical and jubilee years, the time of the land’s sanctity, when holiness can be brought even into inanimate things and the element of earth. This comes through repentance: a person recognizes his lowliness, and his soul becomes like dust before all. Through the intensity of his bitterness, he comes to loathe his life when he recognizes the enormity of his sin in defying the will of the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, until even the existence of his earthly body is nullified “before the dread of God and the splendor of His majesty.” Through this, the element of earth and the inanimate realm throughout the entire world are rectified. For everything is included in the human being: the whole world was created for his sake and to accompany him, as stated in Berakhot 6b. Through his rectification and perfection, the entire world is perfected.
records.explanation: Here Rav Tzadok makes the consequence of creation’s inclusion in the human being explicit: personal rectification can repair the corresponding aspect of the world. In the surrounding argument, “through this” refers to repentance and the humility it produces. This connection is useful specifically when the originating passage concerns the person’s relation to all creation or the effect of his spiritual rectification.

Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This one is equal in worth to the entire world. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says—and some say that Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma says: The entire world was created only to accompany this one.
records.targetHebrew: וְדָבָר זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר: לִהְיוֹת אֶחָד לְמַטָּה וְנִפְרָדִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי אֵין יִחוּד אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁמְּיוּחָדִים בִּמְקוֹרָם בַּה׳ אֶחָד, וְהוּא הַמְאַחֵד כָּל הַנִּבְרָאִים אֲבָל בְּעָלְמָא דְּפֵירוּדָא שֶׁנִּפְרָדִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, הֵם נִפְרָדִים זֶה מִזֶּה גַּם כֵּן וְרַק אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִכִּיר יִחוּד הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְנִקְרָא ״אֹהֲבִי״ (יְשַׁעְיָה מ״א:ח׳) עַל יְדֵי אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ זוֹכֶה גַּם כֵּן לְאַהֲבַת הַבְּרִיּוֹת, שֶׁכָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא לְצַוּוֹת לוֹ (בְּרָכוֹת ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳) שֶׁכְּמוֹ שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יְחִידִי בָּעֶלְיוֹנִים, כָּךְ הוּא יָחִיד בַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים כְּאָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹדֶם הַחֵטְא וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ״א:ה׳) עַל פָּסוּק ״[הֵן] הָאָדָם הָיָה כְּאַחַד מִמֶּנּוּ״ (בְּרֵאשִׁית ג:כב) וְכָל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ הֵם אֵבְרֵי קוֹמָתוֹ, וְזָכָה לְהוֹלִיד ״גּוֹי אֶחָד״
records.targetEnglish: It is impossible to be united below while separated from the blessed God. For unity exists only when beings are united at their source in the one God, who unites all created beings. In the world of separation, however, when they are separated from the blessed God, they are also separated from one another. Only Abraham our patriarch, peace be upon him, who recognized the unity of the blessed God and was called “My beloved,” through love of the blessed God also attains love of created beings. The entire world was created only to accompany him, as stated in Berakhot 6b. Just as the blessed God is unique above, so he is unique below, like Adam before the sin, as the Sages said in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 21, on the verse “The man has become like one of us.” The entire world consists of the limbs of his stature, and he merited to beget “one nation.”
records.explanation: Rav Tzadok explains how love of God becomes love of created beings: their unity comes from their common divine source. This gives the Gemara’s “companionship” a precise spiritual basis and distinguishes it from the attempted unity of the Tower generation discussed immediately before it.

records.sourceHebrew: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ, אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל אָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם — דְּבָרָיו נִשְׁמָעִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״סוֹף דָּבָר הַכֹּל נִשְׁמָע אֶת הָאֱלֹהִים יְרָא וְגוֹ׳״.
records.sourceEnglish: Rabbi Chelbo said in the name of Rav Huna: Any person who has fear of Heaven—his words are heeded, as it is stated: “The end of the matter, everything is heard: fear God,” and so forth.
records.targetHebrew: עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהוּא יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים יוּכַל לְהַכְנִיס בָּהֶם חַיּוּת כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּרָכוֹת ו׳ עַמּוּד ב׳): ״מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם — דְּבָרָיו נִשְׁמָעִים״ הַיְינוּ שֶׁיּוּכַל לְהַכְנִיס חַיּוּת בַּשּׁוֹמֵעַ עַל יְדֵי דִּבּוּרָיו, שֶׁהַדִּבּוּר בּוֹ חַיּוּת הָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: ״לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה״ — ״לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא״ (אוּנְקְלוֹס בְּרֵאשִׁית ב:ז) אֶלָּא שֶׁהַסָּכָל יַרְבֶּה דְּבָרִים, דִּבְרֵי מוֹתָר שֶׁהֵם דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים, רָצָה לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם חַיּוּת אֲבָל יְרֵא שָׁמַיִם הוּא הַמּוּגְדָּר מִפְּנֵי פַּחַד ה׳ הַחוֹפְפוֹ, שֶׁכָּל פְּעוּלוֹתָיו וְדִבּוּרָיו כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ דְּעַל יְדֵי זֶה יֵשׁ בָּהֶם חַיּוּת כְּטַעַם ״וְאַתָּה מְחַיֶּה אֶת כֻּלָּם״ (נְחֶמְיָה ט:ו) יוּכַל בִּדְבוּרָיו וְכֵן בִּפְעוּלוֹתָיו לְהַכְנִיס חַיּוּת גַּם כֵּן בְּאַחֵר:
records.targetEnglish: Through being God-fearing, he can impart vitality to them, as stated in Berakhot 6b: “One who has fear of Heaven—his words are heeded.” This means that through his words he can impart vitality to the listener, for human vitality resides in speech, as “a living soul” is translated by Onkelos as “a speaking spirit.” The fool, however, multiplies words: superfluous words that are idle, meaning that they have no vitality. But the God-fearing person is restrained by the fear of God that rests upon him, so that all his actions and words accord with the will of the blessed God. Through this they possess vitality, in the sense of “You give life to them all,” and he can also impart vitality to another through his words and his actions.
records.explanation: Rav Tzadok interprets “his words are heeded” as more than persuasiveness: speech aligned with God’s will carries spiritual life to its listener. The contrast with idle speech explains why fear of Heaven, rather than verbal skill alone, is the relevant condition in this particular Gemara.

records.sourceHebrew: מַאי ״כִּי זֶה כׇּל הָאָדָם״? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה. רַבִּי אַבָּא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: שָׁקוּל זֶה כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן עַזַּאי אוֹמֵר, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן זוֹמָא אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא לִצְווֹת לָזֶה.
records.sourceEnglish: What is meant by “for this is the whole of man”? Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: The entire world was created only for the sake of this one. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This one is equal in worth to the entire world. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says—and some say that Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma says: The entire world was created only to accompany this one.
records.targetHebrew: ואז יתפלל, מותר לו להתפלל על צרכיו צרכי הגוף, כיון שקיבל עליו עול מלכות שמים שלימה וסילק כל נגיעתו, ממילא כל צרכיו הם רק כדי שיהיה ביכולתו לקיים את רצון השי"ת, ואין לו שום נגיעה מצידו. וכמו שראינו גבי אברהם אבינו ע"ה שהיה מברר עצמו וסילק נגיעת עוה"ז, אז ראה מפורש שכל העולם כולו לא נברא אלא לצוות לזה, כדאיתא במדרש (רבה לך ל"ט) אפילו ספינות שהיו מפרשות בים הגדול היה מתברכות בשביל אאע"ה. ופריך והלא של נסך הם, ומתרץ חלא מוזיל חמרא, היינו כיון שבירר עצמו וסילק כל נגיעת עוה"ז, ממילא היה כל צרכיו כבוד שמים.
records.targetEnglish: “And then he should pray”: he is permitted to pray for his needs, his bodily needs, because once he has accepted the full yoke of the kingdom of Heaven and removed all his personal interest, all his needs are consequently only so that he will be able to fulfill the will of the blessed God; he has no personal interest of his own. Likewise, we see that when Abraham our patriarch, peace be upon him, clarified himself and removed his personal interest in this world, he then saw clearly that the entire world had been created only to accompany this one. As stated in Bereishit Rabbah, Lech Lecha 39, even ships sailing on the Great Sea were blessed for the sake of Abraham our patriarch. The Midrash asks: Were they not carrying wine of idolatrous libation? It answers: Vinegar makes wine cheaper. This means that, because he had clarified himself and removed all his personal interest in this world, all his needs were consequently for the honor of Heaven.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef supplies an important condition for the teaching about the world serving the righteous person: his needs have become directed toward divine service after self-interest has been removed. The passage illuminates uses of the Gemara concerning bodily needs, prayer, and how material support can serve holiness.

records.sourceEnglish: What is meant by “for this is the whole of man”? Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: The entire world was created only for the sake of this one. Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This one is equal in worth to the entire world. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says—and some say that Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma says: The entire world was created only to accompany this one.
records.targetHebrew: בזה מראה לנו ר' יוחנן עד היכן שיש השגחה פרטית על כל דבר, שמטר בשביל יחיד, והיינו שאם צריך לאחד פרט טובה משפיע לו השי"ת. ופרנסה בשביל רבים היינו, שאם אחד מברר עצמו כל כך שכל העולם כולו כדאי לו, אז מראה לו השי"ת שכל העולם כולו לא נברא אלא לצוות לזה, היינו שכל העולם יש להם טובה בזכותו. וזה מורה פרנסה בשביל רבים, שכל צרכיו נחשבים צרכי רבים. וכדאיתא במדרש (רבה לך לט) אפילו ספינות שהיו מפרשות בים הגדול היו נתברכות בשביל אברהם אבינו ופריך המדרש והלא של נסך הם ומתרץ חלא מוזיל חמרא. היינו שלזה האדם מראה השי"ת, שכל דבר נברא רק שיהיה לו לצוותא. וזה הוא התירוץ שמתרץ הגמ' שאני משה כיון דלרבים בעי כרבים דמיא. מאחר שמשה רבינו ע"ה היה לו גודל מסירות נפש בעד כלל ישראל, שלא הכיר מצדו בשום שלימות בעת שהיה חסר אצל ישראל שום טובה ולזה אמר כאן הגמ' כיון דלרבים בעי כרבים דמיא.
records.targetEnglish: Through this Rabbi Yochanan shows us how far individual providence extends over every matter: rain comes for the sake of an individual. That is, if one individual needs a benefit, the blessed God bestows it upon him. “Sustenance comes for the sake of the many” means that if a person clarifies himself to such a degree that the whole world is worthy of existing for him, the blessed God then shows him that the entire world was created only to accompany this one—that is, the whole world receives benefit through his merit. This is the meaning of “sustenance for the sake of the many”: all his needs are counted as the needs of the many. As stated in Bereishit Rabbah, Lech Lecha 39, even ships sailing on the Great Sea were blessed for Abraham our patriarch’s sake. The Midrash asks: Were they not carrying wine of idolatrous libation? It answers: Vinegar makes wine cheaper. The blessed God shows this person that each thing was created to provide him with companionship. This is the Gemara’s answer: “Moses is different; since he sought it for the many, he is considered like the many.” Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, had such great self-sacrifice for the community of Israel that he recognized no perfection of his own while Israel lacked any benefit. For this reason the Gemara says here: “Since he sought it for the many, he is considered like the many.”
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains that creation’s service to the righteous person also benefits others: his needs count as public needs because he cannot regard himself as complete while Israel lacks good. This is a substantive expansion of “to accompany this one” when the originating discussion concerns providence, communal responsibility, or the righteous person’s effect upon the world.

records.targetRef: Tiferet Yosef, The Seventh Day of Pesach 5
records.targetHebrew: והיינו מאחר שישראל אחר כל הגדרים וצמצומים שעובד את השי"ת, ואחר כל העבודות מכיר שאפילו זה הכח שעבד את השי"ת ג"כ הוא שהשי"ת נתן לו זה הכח לעבוד אותו, ואינו נוטל לעצמו שום כח, רק מכיר שהכל הוא מן השי"ת, ממילא מזה ראיה ששוכן השי"ת אצלו. וכדאיתא בזוה"ק (תרומה קכח:) מנא ידעינן דקוב"ה אתרעי' ביה בבר נש ושויה מדוריה ביה כד חזינן דרדיף אבתריה בכל לבא ובכל נפשא. מזה ראיה שהשי"ת שוכן אצלו ויש לו קנין בכל העבודות. וכדאיתא במדרש (תנחומא בהר א) מכרתי את כל העולם לאברהם אבינו ולא הוניתי אותו וחזר והקנה אותו לי. וכמו שאמר כבוד אזמו"ר זללה"ה, מאין הוא הסימן שלא הוניתי אותו והקניתי לו את כל העולם כולו. מן חזר והקנה אותו לי, מאחר שנתתי לו כח לחזור הכל לי, מזה ראיה שיש לו קנין בעולם. ואז כשמברר את עצמו, כך רואה איך שכל הבריאה הוא הכל בשבילו, וכל העולם כולו לא נברא אלא לצוות לזה, וכדמצינו במדרש (רבה לך לט) גבי אאע"ה אפילו ספינות שהיו מפרשות בים הגדול היה ניצולות בשביל אברהם אבינו, ופריך והלא של נסך הם, ומתרץ חלא מוזיל חמרא. מאחר שבירר את עצמו שאחר כל העבודות לא נטל לעצמו שום כח רק החזיר הכל להשי"ת. אז היה הוא עיקר המכוון מהבריאה,
records.targetEnglish: This means that after all the restraints and limitations through which Israel serves the blessed God, and after all the acts of service, a person recognizes that even the strength with which he served the blessed God was itself given to him by the blessed God for that service. He attributes no power to himself, but recognizes that everything comes from the blessed God. This itself is evidence that the blessed God dwells with him. As stated in the Zohar, Terumah 128b: How do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, desires a person and makes His dwelling in him? When we see that he pursues Him with all his heart and all his soul. This is evidence that the blessed God dwells with him and that he has acquired a share in all his acts of service. As stated in Midrash Tanchuma, Behar 1: “I sold the whole world to Abraham our patriarch and did not defraud him; he, in turn, conveyed it back to Me.” My honored grandfather, of blessed memory, said: What shows that “I did not defraud him” and truly conveyed the whole world to him? The fact that “he, in turn, conveyed it back to Me.” Since I gave him the power to return everything to Me, this proves that he has an acquired share in the world. When he clarifies himself in this way, he sees that the entire creation is for his sake and that the whole world was created only to accompany this one. Likewise, Bereishit Rabbah, Lech Lecha 39, states regarding Abraham our patriarch that even ships sailing on the Great Sea were saved for his sake. It asks: Were they not carrying wine of idolatrous libation? It answers: Vinegar makes wine cheaper. Because, after all his acts of service, he clarified himself by attributing no power to himself but returning everything to the blessed God, he became the principal intended purpose of creation.
records.explanation: This passage explains why the Gemara’s teaching need not become a claim of self-importance. Tiferet Yosef places it after recognition that even the power to serve God was received from Him; the person’s relation to all creation is discovered through returning everything to its source. It is relevant where Rav Tzadok discusses self-nullification, divine assistance, or the righteous person as creation’s purpose.

records.sourceHebrew: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ כִּשְׁגָגוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שׁוּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ כִּי כָשַׁלְתָּ בַּעֲוֹנֶךָ״, הָא ״עָוֹן״ — מֵזִיד הוּא, וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ מִכְשׁוֹל. אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ כִּזְכִיּוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְשׁוּב רָשָׁע מֵרִשְׁעָתוֹ וְעָשָׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה עֲלֵיהֶם (חָיֹה) יִחְיֶה״! לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן מֵאַהֲבָה, כָּאן מִיִּרְאָה.
records.sourceEnglish: Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance, for intentional sins are counted for him as unintentional sins, as it is stated: “Return, Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled through your iniquity.” Iniquity is intentional, yet it is called a stumbling. Is this so? Did Reish Lakish not say: Great is repentance, for intentional sins are counted for him as merits, as it is stated: “When a wicked person turns from his wickedness and performs justice and righteousness, because of these he shall live”? There is no difficulty: the latter refers to repentance out of love, and the former to repentance out of fear.

records.targetEnglish: The essence of repentance is to reach the point where God illuminates a person’s eyes so that intentional sins become merits. This means that he recognizes and understands that everything in which he sinned was also within the will of the blessed God, as in the teaching of our Sages at the end of Berakhot 31b concerning three verses: “You have turned their hearts backward,” “that which I have caused to be evil,” and so forth. This accords with the matter of divine knowledge and human choice explained by the Arizal at the end of Arba Me’ot Shekel Kesef: both are true, each in its own domain. In the domain of choice there is no place for divine knowledge, and in the domain of divine knowledge there is, in truth, no place for choice. When he attains this immense light, all his intentional sins return to being within the depths of the blessed God’s knowledge; He, His knowledge, and His will are all one. Since the blessed God willed it so, everything is therefore counted as merit, and the person merits the complete atonement of Yom Kippur. This is the mystery of the goat sent to Azazel. Had a person done this on his own, he would have been committing outright idolatry, falling under “You shall have no other gods,” the foundation of all the prohibitions and of all transgressions and departures from the will of the blessed God. But because the goat is sent by the will of the blessed God, who commands that it be sent to Azazel, this instead becomes a commandment and not a transgression. This is how our Sages explained it in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, chapter 46; see also Ramban on Acharei Mot. We give a portion to Azazel, the evil, because the blessed God commanded that it be given to him. Thus what would be a transgression becomes a commandment.
records.explanation: Rav Tzadok explains the transformation of intentional sins into merits through the illumination reached in repentance. His explicit distinction between the domain of human choice and the domain of divine knowledge is indispensable to the argument, so the whole paragraph is quoted. The Azazel example then explains why an act’s relation to God’s command matters; it does not collapse human choice into advance permission to sin.

records.sourceHebrew: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ כִּשְׁגָגוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שׁוּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ כִּי כָשַׁלְתָּ בַּעֲוֹנֶךָ״, הָא ״עָוֹן״ — מֵזִיד הוּא, וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ מִכְשׁוֹל. אִינִי?! וְהָאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ כִּזְכִיּוֹת, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וּבְשׁוּב רָשָׁע מֵרִשְׁעָתוֹ וְעָשָׂה מִשְׁפָּט וּצְדָקָה עֲלֵיהֶם (חָיֹה) יִחְיֶה״! לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן מֵאַהֲבָה, כָּאן מִיִּרְאָה.
records.sourceEnglish: Reish Lakish said: Great is repentance, for intentional sins are counted for him as unintentional sins, as it is stated: “Return, Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled through your iniquity.” Iniquity is intentional, yet it is called a stumbling. Is this so? Did Reish Lakish not say: Great is repentance, for intentional sins are counted for him as merits, as it is stated: “When a wicked person turns from his wickedness and performs justice and righteousness, because of these he shall live”? There is no difficulty: the latter refers to repentance out of love, and the former to repentance out of fear.

records.targetHebrew:
זכור ימות עולם.
זה מורה, שהשי"ת ציוה לזכור השקליא וטריא שהיה אצלך קודם שבאת אל ישוב הדעת. והדיעות שהיה אצלך מקודם שבאת אל גודל ישוב הדעת, ולא היה אצלך עבודתך בסדר מסודר. בינו שנות דור ודור זה מורה, אחר שבא האדם על סדר עבודה. וכבר הוא אצל בני אדם בסדר מסודר בקביעות. וזה הוא נמי החילוק בין שב מיראה לשב מאהבה כדאיתא בש"ס (יומא פ"ו:) האי עון מזיד הוא וקא קרי ליה כשלון, אלא שב מיראה זדונות נעשות לו כשגגות שב מאהבה נעשות לו כזכיות. ואמר בזה כבוד אזמו"ר זללה"ה ששב מיראה אין פירושו ששב מחמת יראת העונש, אלא מרמז שכבר קנה והשיג אור בשלימות ורק שלא נקבע עוד אצלו בקביעות גמור, ועוד יכול לפסוק ממנו זה האור. וזה מרמז ששב מיראה, שעוד יש לו יראות גדולות שמא יופסק ממנו אור השי"ת מחמת שלא השיג עדיין בסדר מסודר, ושב מאהבה מורה שכבר קבע קדושה אצלו בקביעות כיתד בל תמוט, וכבר השיג אור השי"ת בסדר מסודר:
records.targetEnglish: “Remember the days of old.” This indicates that the blessed God commanded you to remember the debate and deliberation within you before you came to settled understanding, and the opinions you held before you attained great settled understanding, when your service was not yet arranged in an orderly way. “Understand the years of each generation” points to the stage after a person has arrived at an ordered course of service, which has now become fixed and orderly in his life. This is also the difference between one who repents out of fear and one who repents out of love, as stated in Yoma 86b: “This iniquity is intentional, yet it is called a stumbling.” Rather, for one who repents out of fear, intentional sins become like unintentional sins; for one who repents out of love, they become merits. My honored grandfather, of blessed memory, explained that “one who repents out of fear” does not here mean one who repents because of fear of punishment. It points instead to one who has already acquired and fully attained light, but the light has not yet become completely fixed within him and can still cease. This is what repentance out of fear indicates: he still has great fears that the light of the blessed God may be cut off from him, because he has not yet attained it in a settled order. Repentance out of love indicates that he has already established holiness within himself permanently, like a peg that will not move, and has attained the light of the blessed God in an ordered way.
records.explanation: Tiferet Yosef gives a precise inner reading of the Gemara’s contrast between repentance out of fear and repentance out of love. In the explanation he transmits from his grandfather, fear concerns losing an attained divine illumination, while love describes holiness becoming established. The full argument is included so that this interpretive reading is not mistaken for a bare dictionary definition of fear or love.
